root_cause.text: The LED class registration code in `drivers/leds/led-class.c` added a `led_classdev` to `leds_list` before `led_init_core()` initialized `set_brightness_work`, creating a race where default-trigger setup could queue an uninitialized work item.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list)` from before `led_init_core(led_cdev);` to after it, and the CVE description says this early list insertion let `led_trigger_register()`/`led_trigger_set()` call `led_set_brightness()` and queue the “*uninitialized* `led_classdev.set_brightness_work`.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the premature addition of the LED device to the global list during registration.
intent_record.what: The code removes the block in `led_classdev_register_ext()` that acquired `leds_list_lock` and added `led_cdev->node` to `leds_list`; the subsequent `max_brightness` initialization remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: After this change, the LED class device is no longer inserted into the global LED list at this point in the function, so registration no longer publishes the device through that list here. Any behavior that depended on early list visibility is prevented, while the later brightness default assignment still occurs.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add newly registered LED class devices to the global LED list under lock during registration.
intent_record.what: The function `led_classdev_register_ext()` now acquires `leds_list_lock` with `down_write()`, appends `led_cdev->node` to the global `leds_list` using `list_add_tail()`, and then releases the lock with `up_write()` immediately after `led_init_core(led_cdev)` and before the `CONFIG_LEDS_TRIGGERS` block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, newly registered LED class devices are now inserted into the global LED device list in a synchronized way, making them visible to list consumers and preventing concurrent list corruption during registration.

grouping_result.intent: Remove the premature addition of the LED device to the global list during registration.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the early insertion of the LED class device into the global list before initialization completes, which is what allowed default-trigger setup to race with uninitialized work.

The root cause is the ordering/race around LED class device registration and list insertion before core initialization. This change also modifies registration to add LEDs to the global list under lock, directly affecting the vulnerable registration path and concurrency behavior.

candidates.rationale: This prematurely exposes the newly registered LED device to global iteration before led_init_core() has initialized set_brightness_work, enabling default-trigger setup to reach the object and queue an uninitialized work item.

This is the operation that can run after the LED is made visible too early; it may access the partially initialized led_cdev and queue brightness work before led_init_core() has set up set_brightness_work.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement exposes the newly registered LED class device on the global leds_list before led_init_core() has initialized set_brightness_work, which allows default-trigger setup to find the object too early and queue an uninitialized work item.

This call can run while the LED device is still only partially initialized; if the device was added to the global list too early, default-trigger handling may operate on led_cdev before set_brightness_work is initialized.

Author: Richard Purdie <rpurdie@rpsys.net>
Date:   Fri Mar 31 02:31:04 2006 -0800

    [PATCH] LED: add LED class
    
    Add the foundations of a new LEDs subsystem.  This patch adds a class which
    presents LED devices within sysfs and allows their brightness to be
    controlled.
    
    Signed-off-by: Richard Purdie <rpurdie@rpsys.net>
    Cc: Russell King <rmk@arm.linux.org.uk>
    Cc: Greg KH <greg@kroah.com>
    Signed-off-by: Andrew Mor
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is present in this implementation: in `led_classdev_register()` the LED is exposed to the subsystem by `class_device_create(...)`, then `class_device_create_file(...)`, and only after that it is added to the global list with `list_add_tail(&led_cdev->node, &leds_list);`. The root cause says the class registration added a `led_classdev` to `leds_list` before `led_init_core()` initialized `set_brightness_work`, allowing default-trigger setup to queue uninitialized work. This snippet shows the add-to-list happens during registration, but there is no visible initialization of `set_brightness_work` or any ordering fix to ensure it is initialized before list insertion. Therefore the buggy construct is present and the fix is not present in this commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the fix for the reported race. In this version, `led_trigger_set_default(led_cdev);` is still present, but it is moved to occur only after successful creation of the trigger sysfs file: `rc = class_device_create_file(... &class_device_attr_trigger); if (rc) goto err_out_led_list; led_trigger_set_default(led_cdev);`. This means default-trigger setup can no longer run before trigger-related initialization has succeeded. The earlier vulnerable pattern described in the root cause—adding the LED to `leds_list` and then calling `led_trigger_set_default()` before the work initialization was safe—is not present in this snippet as the relevant ordering issue has been corrected. The added error handling and cleanup paths (`err_out_led_list`, `class_device_unregister`) further indicate the fix is already applied.
